title: Primitive Types, Strings, and Input
summary: Use primitive types, String, explicit numeric conversion, Scanner input, arithmetic, and predictable equality rules.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply the Java behavior taught in Primitive Types, Strings, and Input
Compile, run, and test the behavior with observable evidence
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Java primitive types store numeric, boolean, and character values; reference types such as `String` refer to objects. Choose `int` or `long` according to range and `double` for approximate decimal calculations, not exact currency. Integer division discards the fractional part when both operands are integers. `Scanner` token methods and `nextLine` interact with line endings, so design input consistently. Use `.equals` for String value comparison; `==` compares primitive values but reference identity for objects. Parse text with methods such as `Integer.parseInt` and handle invalid input explicitly.
keyPoints: Java primitive types store numeric, boolean, and character values; reference types such as `String` refer to objects.
commonMistakes: double is approximate and unsuitable for exact currency rules
casting only after integer division cannot restore the fraction
